rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is reportedly Medinan and parallels 52:48 in meaning and a closely similar context.
rows.anchor: والآية - على ما روي - مدنية والآية - كما ترى - متحدة المعنى مع قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's abuse by hypocrites, diseased-hearted people, and weak believers was no less than the abuse by Meccan polytheists, as his biography shows.
rows.anchor: الذي كان يلقاه النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من أذى المنافقين والذين في قلوبهم مرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sin and disbelief are not confined to Meccan polytheists; other unbelievers existed, and the Qur'an also attributes sin to groups of Muslims.
rows.anchor: ولا دليل أيضا على انحصار الإثم والكفور في مشركي مكة فهناك غيرهم من الكفار

rows.speaker: محمد الباقر
rows.claim: Asked about “not a mentioned thing,” al-Baqir says the human was something but was not mentioned.
rows.anchor: سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن قوله { لم يكن شيئا مذكورا } قال كان شيئا

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq gives the same explanation: the human existed but was not mentioned.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الأعلى مولى آل سام عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام مثله

rows.speaker: محمد الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says the human was known in divine knowledge, but not yet present in creation; the author explains that he then became created and publicly mentioned.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد الحذاء عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال كان مذكورا في العلم ولم يكن مذكورا في الخلق

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq calls the human decreed but unmentioned; the author says this agrees with the preceding report.
rows.anchor: عن مالك الجهني عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام في الآية قال كان مقدرا غير مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi reports distinguish human knowledge from God's knowledge: one says the person was in neither knowledge nor remembrance, meaning among people; another says he was in God's knowledge but unmentioned among people.
rows.anchor: معنى الحديث الأول أنه لم يكن في علم الناس ولا فيمن يذكرونه فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: أبو الجارود
rows.claim: Al-Jarud reports from al-Baqir that “mingled fluids” means the man's and woman's fluids mixed together.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { امشاج نبتليه } قال ماء الرجل والمرأة اختلطا جميعا

rows.speaker: حمران بن أعين
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq explains that taking the guided path makes one grateful, while leaving it makes one an unbeliever; Qummi and Tawhid reports give similar wording.
rows.anchor: عن حمران بن أعين قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قوله عز وجل { إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا } قال إما آخذ فهو شاكر وإما تارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verses may suggest that spirit and body are two separate realities, with life when joined and death when separated, the person taken at death is the whole human, not one part of a composite.
rows.anchor: جعل الجسد بعينه إنسانا لا ضم واحد إلى واحد آخر يغايره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breathing spirit into the body makes that very body a human being; it does not join two independently distinct entities, so the human remains one reality with or without bodily attachment.
rows.anchor: المراد بنفخ الروح في الجسد جعل الجسد بعينه إنسانا لا ضم واحد إلى واحد آخر يغايره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 23:12–14, the same drop develops through the stages of clot, lump, bones, and flesh before becoming a new creation, supporting human continuity through transformation.
rows.anchor: هو النطفة التي تكونت علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification “mentioned” implies that the human was already something, such as earth or a drop, but was not yet mentioned as this particular person; he then became himself.
rows.anchor: فتقييد الشيء المنفي بالمذكور يعطي أنه كان شيئا لكن لم يكن مذكورا فقد كان أرضا أو نطفة مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is one real entity and the sole source of bodily and spiritual effects, yet is immaterial in himself, as verses about the soul's taking indicate.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان حقيقة واحدة حين تعلق روحه ببدنه وبعد مفارقة روحه البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep as sabat is rest: bodily animal faculties become quiet and recover from the fatigue caused by the soul's activity during wakefulness.
rows.anchor: السبات الراحة والدعة فإن في المنام سكوتا وراحة للقوى الحيوانية البدنية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported lexical reading takes sabat as cutting, since sleep cuts off the soul's actions in the body; the author considers this close to rest.
rows.anchor: وقيل السبات بمعنى القطع وفي النوم قطع التصرفات النفسانية في البدن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some identify sabat with death because 6:60 calls sleep a taking; the author rejects this as remote because the Qur'an distinguishes sleeping souls from those that have died.
rows.anchor: وقد عد سبحانه النوم من الموت حيث قال وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is a garment that covers visible things with darkness and thereby prompts rest, stillness, and return to one's home and family.
rows.anchor: أي ساترا يستر الأشباء بما فيه من الظلمة الساترة للمبصرات كما يستر اللباس البدن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret night as a garment for the day, making it easy to remove; the author dismisses this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أن المراد بكون الليل لباسا كونه كاللباس للنهار يسهل إخراجه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raghib says ʿaysh means animal life, unlike ḥayāt, which can describe God and angels; maʿāsh here is a time or place for living and seeking God's bounty.
rows.anchor: غير أن العيش يختص بحياة الحيوان فلا يقال عيشه تعالى وعيش الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another grammatical reading takes maʿāsh as a verbal noun with an omitted word: the day is made a pursuit of livelihood.
rows.anchor: والتقدير وجعلنا النهار طلب معاش أي مبتغى معاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven strong structures are the seven heavens, firmly built.
rows.anchor: أي سبع سماوات شديدة في بنائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blazing lamp is the sun, intense in both light and heat.
rows.anchor: الوهاج شديد النور والحرارة والمراد بالسراج الوهاج الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʿṣirāt are rain clouds, while thajjāj means water pouring abundantly.
rows.anchor: المعصرات السحب الماطرة وقيل الرياح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some identify al-muʿṣirāt as winds that compress clouds to produce rain; on this reading min should mean bi.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرياح التي تعصر السحب لتمطر والثجاج الكثير الصب للماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water brings forth grain and vegetation that provide food for people and other animals.
rows.anchor: أي حبا ونباتا يقتات بهما الإنسان وسائر الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Interwoven gardens” is coordinated with grain; their trees are densely entwined with one another.
rows.anchor: وجنات ألفاف أي ملتفة أشجارها بعضها ببعض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say alfāf is a plural with no singular form from the same word.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الألفاف جمع لا واحد له من لفظه

rows.speaker: بعض الأخبار
rows.claim: Some reports identify the “great tidings” as Ali, an esoteric interpretation.
rows.anchor: في بعض الأخبار أن النبأ العظيم علي عليه السلام وهو من البطن

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: In the al-Khisal report, the Prophet says that Hūd, al-Wāqiʿa, al-Mursalāt, and al-Nabaʾ made his hair turn gray.
rows.anchor: شيبتني هود والواقعة والمرسلات وعم يتساءلون

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Bakr told the Prophet his hair had grayed quickly, prompting the Prophet's reply about the surahs that caused it.
rows.anchor: شيبتني هود والواقعة والمرسلات وعم يتساءلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary says the earth is spread out as a resting place for humans, and mountains are its pegs.
rows.anchor: قال يمهد فيها الإنسان { والجبال أوتادا } أي أوتاد الأرض

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A saying in Nahj al-Balagha describes rocks as pegs that steady the earth's swaying.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام ووتد بالصخور ميدان أرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi gloss that night clothes the day means night hides what daylight reveals.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد به أنه يخفي ما يظهره النهار ويستر ما يكشفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary identifies the blazing lamp as the shining sun.
rows.anchor: قال الشمس المضيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary glosses al-muʿṣirāt as clouds and thajjāj as successive pouring.
rows.anchor: قال من السحاب { ماء ثجاجا } قال صبا على صب

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq reads yuʿṣirūn in the rain year as “they are rained upon,” citing 78:14; the author identifies the verb as passive and al-muʿṣirāt as clouds that rain.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون بالياء يمطرون

rows.speaker: علي بن معمر
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits a similar explanation from Ali ibn Maʿmar and his father, and Qummi transmits it from Ali.
rows.anchor: وروى العياشي مثل الحديث عن علي بن معمر عن أبيه عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This section describes the promised Day of Decision, what happens to the transgressors and the godfearing, and concludes with a warning.
rows.anchor: تصف الآيات يوم الفصل الذي أخبر به إجمالا

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines mīqāt as the endpoint of a fixed measure of time at which an event occurs, formed from waqt as mīʿād is from waʿd.
rows.anchor: الميقات منتهى المقدار المضروب لحدوث أمر من الأمور وهو من الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision divides judgment among people so each group receives what its deeds merit; kāna and the emphatic inna show that God knew and fixed this endpoint when creating the cosmos.
rows.anchor: فهو ميقات وحد مضروب لفصل القضاء بينهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says afwāj are groups that pass by swiftly.
rows.anchor: والأفواج جمع فوج وهي الجماعة المارة المسرعة على ما ذكره الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the audience as they come in groups continues the warning and alludes to 17:71, where each people is called with its imam.
rows.anchor: وكأن الآية ناظرة إلى قوله تعالى يوم ندعوا كل أناس بإمامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened sky connects the human realm to the angelic realm.
rows.anchor: فاتصل به عالم الإنسان بعالم الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatives construe the phrase as “having doors” or as new paths through the sky; the author finds both readings unsupported.
rows.anchor: وقيل صار فيها طرق ولم يكن كذلك من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirage literally suggests deceptive shining water, and figuratively anything seeming real but lacking reality; here the latter sense is likely.
rows.anchor: ويطلق على كل ما يتوهم ذا حقيقة ولا حقيقة له على طريق الاستعارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains' movement and crushing naturally scatter their parts and erase their shape, producing the image of a mirage.
rows.anchor: أن تسيير الجبال ودكها ينتهي بالطبع إلى تفرق أجزائها وزوال شكلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creative word is existence as it depends on and stands by Him; Jesus is called His word and a spirit from Him because He gave him to Mary outside ordinary causes, as 3:59 analogizes to Adam.
rows.anchor: فبين أنه كلمة الإيجاد التي هي الوجود من حيث انتسابه إليه تعالى وقيامه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an usually mentions spirit with a possessive restriction but also describes an unqualified spirit; 97:4 presents it as an independent heavenly creation distinct from angels, echoed by 70:4.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنها موجود مستقل وخلق سماوي غير الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human spirit is “from” God's spirit, indicating origin; the spirit given to believers is a means of divine support, while the prophets receive the Holy Spirit as strengthening and purification.
rows.anchor: الدالة على المبدئية وسماه نفخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirits attributed to humans, believers, prophets, and angels emanate from the absolute Spirit as overflow or shadow from its source, always by God's permission.
rows.anchor: نسبة الروح المضافة التي في هذه الآيات إلى الروح المطلقة المذكورة في سورة القدر نسبة الإفاضة إلى المفيض والظل إلى ذي الظل بإذن الله

rows.speaker: موسى الكاظم
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports al-Kazim identifying the permitted speakers on Judgment Day as the Imams: they glorify God, bless the Prophet, and intercede for their followers, and God accepts their intercession.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الحسن الماضي عليه السلام قال قلت { يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا لا يتكلمون } الآية

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ transmits a similar report from al-Sadiq through al-Ayyashi and Muawiya ibn Ammar.
rows.anchor: ورواه في المجمع عن العياشي مرفوعا عن معاوية بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report names one instance of permitted intercession; angels, prophets, believers, and witnesses from other communities may also speak by permission.
rows.anchor: الرواية من قبيل ذكر بعض المصاديق فهناك شفعاء أخر من الملائكة والأنبياء والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first three oaths describe angels descending amid competing causes; the appointed angel hurries to complete the cause decreed by God, while the remaining terms describe their swift departure, arrival, and management.
rows.anchor: فالملائكة ينزلون على الأشياء وقد تجمعت عليها الأسباب وتنازعت فيها وجودا وعدما وبقاء وزوالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five oaths portray the angels' assigned dispositions as they manage a worldly event from descent through completion, pointing to angelic governance and supporting resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: فالآيات الخمس إقسام بما يتلبس به الملائكة من الصفات عندما يؤمرون بتدبير أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels mediate between God and things in both origination and return, operating as causes above material causes before death and in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الملائكة وسائط بينه تعالى وبين الأشياء بدء وعودا على ما يعطيه القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return-stage mediation includes taking souls, grave questioning and recompense, trumpet death and revival, gathering, books, scales, judgment, and admission to Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: وقبض الروح إجراء السؤال وثواب القبر وعذابه وإماتة الكل بنفخ الصور وإحيائهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels also mediate revelation, guard it from Satan, support the Prophet, and strengthen and seek forgiveness for believers.
rows.anchor: وكذا وساطتهم في مرحلة التشريع من النزول بالوحي ودفع الشياطين عن المداخلة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oaths and 35:1 portray angels as messengers with wings, created to mediate God's commands to creation, as 21:26–27 and 16:50 say they obey and act only on His order.
rows.anchor: في أنهم خلقوا وشأنهم أن يتوسطوا بينه تعالى وبين خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angelic mediation is a regular divine pattern, not an occasional device that God may arbitrarily bypass; God's way does not change or divert.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك على سبيل الاتفاق بأن يجري الله سبحانه أمرا بأيديهم ثم يجري مثله لا بتوسيطهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels have ranks, and higher angels can direct lower ones; their delegated actions still carry God's command, as when the Angel of Death assigns assistants.
rows.anchor: ومن الوساطة كون بعضهم فوق بعض مقاما وأمر العالي منهم السافل بشيء من التدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angelic and material causation is vertically ordered: a distant cause acts through nearer causes, without competing with God's sole ultimate causality.
rows.anchor: فإن السببية طويلة لا عرضية أي إن السبب القريب سبب للحادث والسبب البعيد سبب للسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This mediation does not grant angels independent control, as pagan delegation theories claim; every created cause lacks independence from God, while scripture affirms both angelic and natural causes.
rows.anchor: وليس لشيء من الأسباب استقلال قباله تعالى حتى ينقطع عنه فيمنع ذلك استناد ما استند إليه إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing illustrates the ordered causes: writing is attributed to the pen and hand, yet the independently acting human is its true cause.
rows.anchor: فمثل الأشياء في استنادها إلى أسبابها المترتبة القريبة والبعيدة وانتهائها إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported reading supplies an omitted object: the warning is a lesson for whoever fears God; the author says the preceding interpretation is more eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقيل المفعول محذوف والتقدير لمن يخشى الله والوجه السابق أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether humans or heaven are harder to create rebukes deniers and answers their doubt: God created what is greater and can recreate humans.
rows.anchor: بأن الله خلق ما هو أشد منكم خلقا فهو على خلقكم وإنشائكم النشأة الأخرى لقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic order's connection to human life also argues for God's lordship, prophecy, obligations, and the resurrection where deeds are repaid, introducing 79:34 onward.
rows.anchor: صحة النبوة وجعل التكاليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rebuke designed to remove the perceived difficulty of resurrection; “He built it” begins a detailed explanation of heaven's creation.
rows.anchor: استفهام توبيخي بداعي رفع استبعادهم البعث بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven's raised height is its elevated ceiling; its leveling arranges and places each part according to wisdom, as in 38:72.
rows.anchor: أي رفع سقفها وما ارتفع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God darkened heaven's night and brought forth its day; ḍuḥā originally means the sun's spread and extended light but here means daytime generally.
rows.anchor: والأصل في معنى الضحى انبساط الشمس وامتداد النهار أريد به مطلق النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are ascribed to heaven because celestial bodies cause their appearance and concealment; the terms cover all dark bodies, not only Earth.
rows.anchor: ولا يختص الليل والنهار بالأرض التي نحن عليها بل يعمان سائر الأجرام المظلمة المستنيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahā means that Earth was spread and extended after heaven was built and ordered; the alternative “along with that” is reported, as is a derivation from rolling.
rows.anchor: أي بسطها ومدها بعد ما بنى السماء ورفع سمكها وسواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing out Earth's water means releasing springs and rivers; its pasture is all vegetation eaten by humans and animals, not only animal fodder.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن المراد بالمرعى مطلق النبات الذي يتغذى به الحيوان والانسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are anchored to stop Earth from swaying and store water and minerals, as other Qur'anic passages indicate.
rows.anchor: أثبتها على الأرض لئلا تميد بكم وادخر فيها المياه والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation and ordering of heaven and Earth provide for humans and their livestock, obligating people to know, fear, and thank their Lord; the greater creation also makes resurrection no difficulty for God.
rows.anchor: فهذا الخلق والتدبير الذي فيه تمتيعكم يوجب عليكم معرفة ربكم وخوف مقامه وشكر نعمته

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says al-ṭāmma is something elevated and overpowering; the word names an irresistible catastrophe.
rows.anchor: والطامة العالية الغالبة يقال هذا أطم من هذا أي أعلى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Greater Calamity is the Resurrection, which overwhelms every other calamity; the opening fa shows that it follows necessarily from the creation and governance just described.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالطامة الكبرى القيامة لأنها داهية تعلو وتغلب كل داهية هائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day the human remembers” is a time phrase describing the arrival of the Calamity, and striving means serious action.
rows.anchor: ظرف لمجيء الطامة الكبرى، والسعي هو العمل بجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is exposed when its cover is removed and all who can see witness it; the verse implies Hell already exists and is unveiled then, while 50:22 is broader in meaning.
rows.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في أن الجحيم مخلوقة قبل يوم القيامة وإنما تظهر يومئذ ظهورا بكشف الغطاء عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.
rows.anchor: وقدم صفة أهل الجحيم لأن وجه الكلام إلى المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgression entails rejecting the afterlife, preferring worldly life, and following the self's desires; the opposite is fear that restrains attachment to the world and forbids following desire.
rows.anchor: كان لما يقابل الطغيان من الوصف وهو الخوف ما يقابل الإيثار واتباع هوى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes restraining the self from desire rather than never acting on it, since ignorance and weakness may cause a sin without arrogance and God is forgiving.
rows.anchor: وإنما أخذ في وصفه النهي عن الهوى دون ترك اتباعه عملا لأن الإنسان ضعيف ربما ساقته الجهالة إلى المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two classes are unbelieving wrongdoers and faithful, pious people; the fate of the weak and those mixing good and bad deeds is left to God, who may forgive or accept intercession.
rows.anchor: وهناك غير الطائفتين طوائف أخر من المستضعفين والذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “the refuge,” the definite article can replace a possessive pronoun, or an omitted pronoun can be supplied: it means the refuge for him.
rows.anchor: على أن تكون اللام عوضا عن الضمير أو الضمير محذوف والتقدير هي المأوى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqām originally means a place or time of standing, but can mean a person's state or rank by extension, as in the cited Qur'anic uses.
rows.anchor: المقام اسم مكان يراد به المكان الذي يقوم فيه جسم من الأجسام وهو الأصل في معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's station as Lord includes the attributes entailed by lordship, such as knowledge, absolute power, dominance, mercy, and wrath; it is the source of forgiveness for believers and punishment for deniers.
rows.anchor: وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The station feared is God's lordship, the source of mercy for faithful people and painful punishment for those who deny and disobey.
rows.anchor: مرحلة ربوبيته التي هي المبدأ لرحمته ومغفرته لمن آمن واتقى ولأليم عذابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says it is the servant's standing before God on Judgment Day to answer for deeds; the author dismisses this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بمقام ربه مقامه من ربه يوم القيامة حين يسأله عن أعماله وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading treats “fearing his Lord's station” as an emphatic insertion meaning simply fearing his Lord, like the phrase “honor his abode.”
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى خاف مقام ربه خاف ربه بطريق الإقحام

rows.speaker: علي بن مهزيار
rows.claim: Al-Fiqh reports al-Baqir saying God may swear by any of His creatures, but creatures may swear only by God; al-Kafi transmits a similar report from al-Baqir.
rows.anchor: قال إن لله عز وجل أن يقسم من خلقه بما شاء وليس لخلقه أن يقسموا إلا به

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets the oaths as angels taking unbelievers' souls, painfully pulling them out, guiding believers' souls upward, racing them to God, and managing people's affairs year by year; the author says this is a possible exemplification and the painful extraction is figurative.
rows.anchor: أخرج سعيد بن المنصور وابن المنذر عن علي في قوله { والنازعات غرقا } قال هي الملائكة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwa about the managers of affairs, Ali says they are angels who manage the remembrance and command of the Merciful.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب أن ابن الكوا سأله عن { المدبرات أمرا } قال الملائكة يدبرون ذكر الرحمن وأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary says the first blast splits Earth and its inhabitants, while the following blast is the cry.
rows.anchor: قال تنشق الأرض بأهلها والرادفة الصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary says Quraysh asked whether they would return after death.
rows.anchor: في قوله { أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة } قال قالت قريش أنرجع بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary glosses their “losing return” statement as mockery.
rows.anchor: في قوله { تلك إذا كرة خاسرة } قال قالوا هذه على حد الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: محمد الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says returning to the first state means a new creation.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قوله { أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة } يقول في الخلق الجديد

rows.speaker: محمد الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir explains al-sāhirah as the earth's surface: people are in graves, then emerge onto the ground when they hear the cry.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله { فإذا هم بالساهرة } والساهرة الأرض كانوا في القبور فلما سمعوا الزجرة

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says that knowing God sees, hears, and knows one's deeds restrains a person from wrongdoing; the author says this supports his interpretation of fearing God's station.
rows.anchor: قال من علم أن الله يراه ويسمع ما يقول

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali warns that following desire turns people away from truth, while long hopes make them forget the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إنما أخاف عليكم الاثنين اتباع الهوى وطول الأمل أما اتباع الهوى فإنه يصد عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers repeated questions about the Hour by saying only God knows when it will come.
rows.anchor: تعرض لسؤالهم عن وقت قيام الساعة ورد له بأن علمه ليس لأحد إلا الله فقد خصه بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect “they ask” suggests ongoing questioning: after hearing about resurrection, the mockers repeatedly demanded a date; marsā is a verbal noun meaning establishment or settling.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن التعبير بيسألونك لإفادة الاستمرار فقد كان المشركون بعد ما سمعوا حديث القيامة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says dhikrā means frequent remembrance and is more emphatic than dhikr; the construction asks what knowledge the Prophet could gain from repeatedly mentioning the Hour.
rows.anchor: والذكرى كثرة الذكر وهو أبلغ من الذكر على ما ذكره الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhikrā is the heart's apprehension of a thing's true nature; the Prophet cannot know the Hour's reality and timing by frequent remembrance, which better fits the context.
rows.anchor: أو الذكرى بمعنى حضور حقيقة معنى الشيء في القلب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the Hour's remembrance is unrelated to the Prophet's mission, which is to warn those who fear it; another says the question is rebuked because his mission is already linked to the Hour and cites a report that he and the Hour were sent close together. The author finds these readings contextually weak and strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى ليس ذكراها مما يرتبط ببعثتك إنما بعثت لتنذر من يخشاها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as part of the polytheists' question about what the Prophet knows from remembering the Hour; the author says the context does not suit it.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية من تمام سؤال المشركين خاطبوا به النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمعنى ما الذي عندك من العلم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's endpoint belongs to God, so only He knows its reality, properties, and appointed time; people should not ask and the Prophet cannot answer.
rows.anchor: فليس لهم أن يسألوا عن وقتها وليس في وسعك أن تجيب عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may also mean that the Hour entails the extinction of things and causes, revealing that dominion belongs to God alone; even time cannot truly delimit it.
rows.anchor: أن الساعة تقوم بفناء الأشياء وسقوط الأسباب وظهور أن لا ملك إلا لله الواحد القهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The only direct Qur'anic temporal limit is the world's extinction and its cosmic upheaval; otherwise the Hour is described figuratively as a brief interval, including in 46:35 and 30:55–56.
rows.anchor: ولذا لم يرد في كلامه تعالى من التحديد إلا تحديد اليوم بانقراض نشأة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour comes suddenly, as 7:187 says; this supports God's exclusive knowledge, though the argument needs further reflection to reconcile other verses.
rows.anchor: ويلوح إلى ما مر ما في مواضع من كلامه أن الساعة لا تأتي إلا بغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commissioned only to warn those disposed to fear the Hour when reminded; he is not commissioned to disclose its time.
rows.anchor: إنما كلفناك بإنذار من يخشى الساعة دون الإخبار بوقت قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusive warning role narrows the Prophet's task and denies that he knows the date; “fear” is readiness to fear upon reminder, not necessarily existing fear before warning.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخشية على ما يناسب المقام الخوف منها إذا ذكر بها أي شأنية الخشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means that worldly life until resurrection will seem as brief as one afternoon or its morning, like a portion of one day.
rows.anchor: بأن قرب الساعة من حياتهم الدنيا بحيث مثلهم حين يرونها مثلهم لو لبثوا بعد حياتهم في الأرض عشية أو ضحى تلك العشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “sojourn” is the interval from worldly life to resurrection, meaning the grave period; counting the whole worldly life for judgment supports this reading.
rows.anchor: أن المراد باللبث لبث ما بين الحياه الدنيا والبعث أي لبثهم في القبور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative makes the sojourn the interval from asking about the Hour until resurrection; the author objects that people witness the interval only at resurrection and that death, not their question, precedes it.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به اللبث بين حين سؤالهم عن وقتها وبين البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites 23:114, which asks how many years people remained on Earth, while rejecting worldly life as the meaning of the brief sojourn.
rows.anchor: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

rows.speaker: محمد الباقر
rows.claim: Qummi reports al-Baqir saying that a servant who can commit a sin but leaves it from fear of God and His prohibition is rewarded with Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال هو العبد إذ وقف على معصية الله وقدر عليها ثم تركها مخافة الله ونهي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary glosses the question as “when does it come?” and says its knowledge belongs to God.
rows.anchor: قال متى تقوم؟ فقال الله { إلى ربك منتهاها } أي علمها عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qummi commentary says the period was part of a day.
rows.anchor: عشية أو ضحاها } قال بعض يوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A weak-chain report says Meccan polytheists mockingly asked the Prophet when the Hour would come, and these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن ابن عباس قال إن مشركي مكة سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا متى تقوم الساعة استهزاء منهم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report graded sound by al-Hakim says the Prophet was repeatedly asked about the Hour until these verses were revealed, after which he was not asked; the author says the context does not fit this as a reply to the Prophet's own question.
rows.anchor: والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه عن عائشة قالت ما زال رسول الله يسأل عن الساعة حتى أنزل عليه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet answered Bedouins by pointing to the youngest person and saying their Hour would come if he lived a century; the author rejects this as an unsuitable date-setting, since revelation repeatedly says only God knows the Hour.
rows.anchor: كانت الأعراب إذا قدموا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سألوه عن الساعة فينظر إلى أحدث إنسان فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open reading “anā” begins a detailed but necessarily incomplete account of God's provisioning of human food; ordinary explanation cannot encompass the full system and its cosmic relations.
rows.anchor: وهو بيان تفصيلي لتدبيره تعالى طعام الإنسان نعم هو مرحلة ابتدائية من التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pouring water means rain falling from above and may include springs and rivers, since underground water stores originate in rain.
rows.anchor: والمراد بصب الماء إنزال الأمطار على الأرض لإنبات النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth splitting is plants breaking through soil; “then” and the following “so” reflect the sequence from rain to growth and grain.
rows.anchor: ظاهره شق الأرض بالنبات الخارج منها ولذا عطف على صب الماء بثم وعطف عليه إنبات الحب بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “in it” refers to Earth; grain means crops such as wheat and barley that people eat, alongside grapes and other listed produce.
rows.anchor: للأرض، والمراد بالحب جنس الحب الذي يقتات به الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadb is fresh, tender greens that people repeatedly cut and eat; an alternative says it is vegetation cut for animal fodder.
rows.anchor: والقضب هو الغض الرطب من البقول الذي يأكله الإنسان يقضب أي يقطع مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens are enclosed orchards, and ghalb describes large, thick trees; thus the phrase means orchards filled with great, sturdy trees.
rows.anchor: فالحدائق الغلب البساتين المشتملة على أشجار عظام غلاظ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take fruit as all fruits, others as fruits excluding grapes and pomegranates; ab is grass or pasture, and the earlier mention of olives and dates may emphasize their importance.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما عدا العنب والرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “provision for you and your livestock” is the purpose for which the produce was grown; the shift to direct address emphasizes the bounty.
rows.anchor: مفعول له أي أنبتنا ما أنبتنا مما تطعمونه ليكون تمتيعا لكم وللأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deafening cry is the trumpet blast and marks the end of general providence, when humans answer for whether they fulfilled the divine call to worship.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ينتهي إليه ما ذكر من التدبير العام الربوبي للانسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People flee their closest family because the overwhelming crisis absorbs all attention, leaving no capacity to care about anyone else.
rows.anchor: فالبلبلة إذا عظمت واشتدت وأطلت على الانسان جذبته إلى نفسها وصرفته عن كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oaths vindicate the Prophet and the Qur'an from charges of madness and satanic interference, affirming that revelation comes through a trustworthy angel; al-khunnas are most likely the five wandering planets.
rows.anchor: فأقرب الأقوال أولها والثاني بعيد والثالث أبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khunnas means withdrawing, jawārī means fast-running, and kunnās means entering a dwelling; the five planets' direct, retrograde, and stationary periods match these traits best.
rows.anchor: فإن لها في حركاتها على ما تشاهد استقامة ورجعة وإقامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation means all stars, which disappear in daylight, travel visibly by night, and set; the author considers it less fitting.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بها مطلق الكواكب وخنوسها استتارها في النهار تحت ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A more remote interpretation identifies the objects as wild cows or gazelles, perhaps as examples of wild animals generally.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بها بقر الوحش أو الظبي ولا يبعد أن يكون ذكر بقر الوحش أو الظبي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says ʿasʿasa can mean the night approaching or retreating, referring to twilight at either edge of night; the link with dawn favors its retreat here.
rows.anchor: والعسعسة تطلق على إقبال الليل وعلى إدباره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view takes ʿasʿasa as the onset of night, but the author finds this distant in context.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بها إقبال الليل وهو بعيد لما عرفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is described as breathing because its light spreads over the horizon and drives darkness away; a person resting after hard labor is the image, which the author finds more intuitive than Zamakhshari's spirit-and-breeze metaphor.
rows.anchor: وعد الصبح متنفسا بسبب انبساط ضوئه على الأفق ودفعه الظلمة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says dawn's arrival brings a spirit and breeze, which are metaphorically its breath.
rows.anchor: قلت إذا أقبل الصبح أقبل بإقباله روح ونسيم

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel lifted four cities of Lot, each with 400,000 fighters besides their children, from the earth until heaven heard their animals, then overturned them; he says his trustworthiness meant never altering a command. The author finds the report problematic and notes Ibn Asakir was criticized, especially for solitary reports.
rows.anchor: ما أحسن ما أثنى عليك ربك ذي قوة عند ذي العرش مكين

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says a person who seeks forgiveness seventy times daily in Shaʿban is recorded in the clear horizon, an area before the Throne with flowing rivers and as many vessels as stars.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من قال في كل يوم من شعبان سبعين مرة أستغفر الله

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq explains “not the word of a banished Satan” as a rejection of Quraysh's soothsayers, whose words were attributed to satans speaking through them.
rows.anchor: أسنده إلى أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قوله { وما هو بقول شيطان رجيم } قال يعني الكهنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited three groups include those brought near to God; weak or suspended people may also fall outside the right- and left-hand groups, as 9:106 suggests.
rows.anchor: فمدلول الآيات خروج المقربين من الفريقين، ومثلهم المستضعفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division into right- and left-hand recipients of the book need not include everyone; the passage names pious people and those condemned to Hell to urge faith and piety.
rows.anchor: فمن الجائز أن لا يكون تقسيم أهل الجمع إلى أصحاب اليمين وأصحاب الشمال تقسيما حاصرا لجميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several surahs similarly present exemplary believers and disbelievers while leaving other classes unstated, to show that piety brings happiness and rebellion brings misery.
rows.anchor: فالغرض فيها ذكر انموذج من أهل الإيمان والطاعة وأهل الكفر والتكذيب والسكوت عمن سواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shafaq is the twilight redness, then yellow, then whiteness that appears in the west early at night.
rows.anchor: الشفق الحمرة ثم الصفرة ثم البياض التي تحدث بالمغرب أول الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night gathers people and animals that spread out by day and return to their homes to rest; an alternative takes wasaq as driving stars from concealment into view.
rows.anchor: أي ضم وجمع ما تفرق وانتشر في النهار من الإنسان والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's light gathers and combines until it is full and round.
rows.anchor: أي اجتمع وانضم بعض نوره إلى بعض فاكتمل نوره وتبدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer says people pass through successive stages that fit together: worldly life, death, the intermediate life, afterlife, final life, reckoning, and recompense.
rows.anchor: والمراد به كيف كان المرحلة بعد المرحلة يقطعها الإنسان في كدحه إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath confirms 84:6 and the report of resurrection, and prepares for the rebuke over disbelief and the warning that follows; human stages are sequential and mutually aligned.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن المراحل التي يقطعها الإنسان في مسيره إلى ربه مترتبة متطابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about why they do not believe or prostrate is a rebuke; the turn from addressing them to speaking of them reflects the Prophet's turning away from their failure to learn.
rows.anchor: الاستفهام للتعجيب والتوبيخ ولذا ناسب الالتفات الذي فيه من الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect “they deny” indicates continued denial; their unbelief explains it, and God knows the disbelief they store in their hearts as they follow their ancestors and leaders.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عنهم بالذين كفروا للدلالة على علة التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret God's knowledge of what they contain as hidden thoughts beyond their denial and shirk, but the author says this is distant from the context.
rows.anchor: أن لهم وراء التكذيب مضمرات في قلوبهم لا يحيط بها العبارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah condemns attachment to worldly life, which leads to tyranny and ingratitude: people mistake wealth for divine favor and poverty for humiliation, though both are tests of what they prepare for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فما يصيبه من القدرة والثروة ومن الفقر وضيق المعاش امتحان وابتلاء إلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment people will realize that wealth, poverty, power, and weakness were tests; they could prepare for the next life but chose punishment over reward.
rows.anchor: وكان يمكنه أن يقدم من يومه لغده فلم يفعل وآثر العقاب على الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salvation belongs to the tranquil soul submitted to God, steady through trials and neither tyrannized by gain nor made ungrateful by loss; the surah is Meccan by its context.
rows.anchor: التي لا تتزلزل بعواصف الابتلاءات ولا يطغيه الوجدان ولا يكفره الفقدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajr is dawn, shafʿ is an even pair, witr is odd, the night passes and withdraws, and ḥijr means intellect; the oath invokes dawn and the following objects.
rows.anchor: الفجر الصبح والشفع الزوج، قال الراغب الشفع ضم الشيء إلى مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajr most likely means dawn generally, though it may mean the dawn of the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah; proposals include the month's dawn, Muharram, Friday, Muzdalifah, prayer, all daylight, or springs, which the author calls poor.
rows.anchor: ولعل ظاهر قوله { والفجر } أن المراد به مطلق الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are probably the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijjah, with the indefinite form used for magnification; alternatives name ten nights in Ramadan or Muharram, or ten nights of worship.
rows.anchor: لعل المراد بها الليالي العشر من أول ذي الحجة إلى عاشرها والتنكير للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even and odd can fit the day of Tarwiyah and the day of ʿArafah, especially if the dawn and ten nights refer to Dhu al-Hijjah.
rows.anchor: يقبل الانطباق على يوم التروية ويوم عرفة وهو الأنسب على تقدير أن يراد بالفجر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternative interpretations take the even and odd as the night prayers of shafʿ and witr, prayer generally, or the sacrifice day and ʿArafah.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد صلاتا الشفع والوتر في آخر الليل، وقيل مطلق الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the even with all creatures because God created them in pairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشفع جميع الخلق لأنه قال
